sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Once a week the open ground beside the bus stand fills with sellers who are absent on the other six days. A woman from an inland village spreads red chillies on a mat; beside her a man sells clay pots, and beyond him someone has brought dried fish, brooms, jaggery and cashew nuts in old biscuit tins. By early afternoon most of it is gone and the ground is empty again.

To an outsider the weekly market looks like a survival from an earlier age, soon to be replaced by shops that open every day. It has lasted because it solves a problem those shops do not. A grower with twenty kilos of chillies cannot supply a supermarket, which wants the same quantity every week of the year, and cannot afford to rent a stall for goods she has only in March. The market asks for nothing but a small fee on the day she comes. It gathers many such small sellers in one place, so that buyers find it worth the journey.

The arrangement has costs. There is no shelter in the rain, little check on weights, and no one to complain to. Improving these things is reasonable. Replacing the market with a permanent building of numbered stalls, as is sometimes proposed, would be something else: it would give the space to exactly those traders who can pay rent all year, and they are not the people the market exists to serve.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: A notice that the public cannot understand has not been issued; it has only been displayed. This is easily forgotten by those who write notices, because to the writer the meaning is obvious. He knows what 'the competent authority' is, which office is meant by 'the undersigned', and what will happen if 'the needful' is not done. The reader standing at the board knows none of these things and has no one to ask.

Writing plainly is sometimes dismissed as a matter of style, a courtesy that busy offices cannot afford. The cost of not doing it is practical. Every unclear notice produces visitors who come on the wrong day, bring the wrong papers, or do not come at all and lose a benefit they were entitled to. Each of them takes up the time of a clerk who must then explain in speech what the notice failed to say in writing.

A useful test is to hand the draft to someone outside the office and ask three questions. Who is this for? What must they do? By when? If the answers are slow in coming, the fault lies with the draft and not with the reader. Legal precision need not be sacrificed. The exact rule can be cited at the foot of the page for those who want it, after the notice has first told everyone else what to do.

questions.q: According to the passage, the weekly market has lasted because:
opts: its goods are cheaper than those in shops
it suits sellers who have small or seasonal quantities to sell
the law protects it from competition
questions.why: It solves a problem daily shops do not: a small grower with goods for only part of the year can sell there for a small fee.

questions.q: Why can the chilli grower not supply a supermarket?
opts: A supermarket wants the same quantity every week of the year
Her village is too far from the town
Her chillies are of poor quality
questions.why: She has twenty kilos, and only in March; a supermarket wants a steady supply all year.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a cost of the weekly market?
questions.why: The market asks for nothing but a small fee. The other three are listed in the last paragraph.

questions.q: The author regards the proposal to build permanent numbered stalls as:
opts: likely to shut out the sellers the market is meant for
the only way to check weights
questions.why: It would give the space to traders who can pay rent all year, who are not the people the market exists to serve.

questions.q: As used in the second paragraph, 'a survival' most nearly means:
opts: something that continues from an earlier time
a means of earning a living
questions.why: To an outsider the market looks like a leftover from an earlier age.

questions.q: The opening sentence means that a notice:
opts: must be signed before it is displayed
achieves its purpose only if its readers understand it
should not be put up on a board
is valid only after it is issued twice
questions.why: Displaying a notice nobody can understand does not amount to informing the public.

questions.q: Why do those who write notices overlook unclear wording?
opts: They are too busy to read their drafts
They are required to use legal terms
They want to confuse the public
The meaning seems obvious to them because they know the terms
questions.why: To the writer the meaning is obvious; he knows what the official phrases refer to.

questions.q: What, according to the passage, is the practical cost of an unclear notice?
opts: People act wrongly or miss benefits, and staff must explain in person
The notice has to be translated
questions.why: Visitors come on the wrong day or with the wrong papers, or lose a benefit, and a clerk must then explain.

questions.q: Under the author's test, if an outsider cannot quickly answer the three questions:
opts: the notice should be withdrawn permanently
the rule itself must be changed
questions.why: If the answers are slow in coming, the fault lies with the draft and not with the reader.

questions.q: How does the author reconcile plain writing with legal precision?
opts: By removing all references to rules
By leaving legal matters to the courts
By citing the exact rule at the foot, after the plain instructions
questions.why: The exact rule can be cited at the foot of the page, after the notice has told readers what to do.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: She is good ______ drafting letters.
questions.why: The adjective 'good' takes 'at' before a skill or activity.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: If he ______ harder, he would pass the test.
questions.why: An unreal present condition uses if + simple past, with 'would' in the main clause.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The teacher made the students ______ the passage twice.
questions.why: After 'make' in the active voice, the verb is used without 'to'.

questions.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? He prefers (A) / tea (B) / than coffee (C) / in the morning (D).
questions.why: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than': prefers tea to coffee.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said to me, 'Where do you work?'
opts: She asked me where did I work.
She asked me where I worked.
She asked me where do you work.
She told me where I worked.
questions.why: A reported question uses statement word order, with the tense shifted back.

questions.q: Which feature will the Census of 2027 have for the first time since Independence?
questions.why: The Census with reference date 1 March 2027 will enumerate caste and will also be the first conducted digitally.

questions.q: The Zilla Panchayat elections held in Goa in December 2025 covered how many seats in all?
questions.why: Fifty seats were contested across the State. The BJP-led alliance won 32 of them.

questions.q: Which country won the FIFA World Cup in 2026?
questions.why: Spain won the tournament, which was hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico.

questions.q: The Dr Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary is on which island in the Mandovi?
questions.why: The sanctuary covers mangrove forest at the western tip of Chorao.

questions.q: The Cumbarjua Canal links which two rivers?
questions.why: The canal joins the Mandovi and the Zuari, which together form Goa's main waterway.

questions.q: How many Lok Sabha seats does Goa have?
questions.why: North Goa and South Goa. The State also has one seat in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to become Chief Minister of Goa, Daman and Diu?
questions.why: Shashikala Kakodkar, daughter of Dayanand Bandodkar, was Chief Minister from 1973 to 1979.

questions.q: The Union, State and Concurrent Lists are contained in which Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.why: The Seventh Schedule divides legislative subjects among the three lists.

questions.q: The Dandi March, which began the Salt Satyagraha, took place in:
questions.why: Gandhi walked from Sabarmati to Dandi in March and April 1930.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.why: The 101st Amendment (2016) enabled GST, which took effect on 1 July 2017.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 100, 96, 88, 76, 60, ?
questions.why: The amounts subtracted are 4, 8, 12, 16, then 20: 60 - 20 = 40.

questions.q: Which letter is eighth to the right of the fifteenth letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.why: The fifteenth letter is O. Eight places on is the twenty-third letter, W.

questions.q: In a certain code PEN is written as QGQ. How is INK written in that code?
questions.why: The letters move forward by 1, 2 and 3 places: I-J, N-P, K-N.

questions.q: 6 is to 42 as 8 is to:
questions.why: 42 is 6 x 7. In the same way 8 x 9 = 72.

questions.q: Introducing a man, a woman said, 'His wife is the only daughter of my father.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.why: The only daughter of her father is the woman herself, so the man is her husband.

questions.q: The Collectorate is due north of the bus stand. The court is due east of the Collectorate. In which direction is the bus stand from the court?
questions.why: From the court, the bus stand lies to the west and to the south, that is, south-west.

questions.q: A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is taller than C. E is shorter than B. When the five are arranged by height, who is in the middle?
questions.why: In descending order: D, C, A, B, E. A is third.

questions.q: Question: Is x greater than y? Statement I: x + y = 10. Statement II: x - y = 2.
opts: The statements are not sufficient even together
questions.why: If x - y = 2, then x is 2 more than y, which answers the question. Statement I alone does not.

questions.q: A bus covers 180 km in 4 hours. At the same speed, how far will it travel in 6 hours?
questions.why: The speed is 45 km/h, so in 6 hours it covers 270 km, not among options A to D.

questions.q: Statement A: Heavy rain fell in the catchment area for three days. Statement B: The water level in the reservoir rose sharply.
opts: A is the cause and B is its effect
B is the cause and A is its effect
Both are effects of independent causes
questions.why: Rain in the catchment fills the reservoir, so A leads to B.

questions.q: Who compiled 'The Guiding Symptoms of our Materia Medica'?
questions.why: Constantine Hering's Guiding Symptoms runs to ten volumes. Kent wrote the Lectures on Homoeopathic Materia Medica, Boericke the Pocket Manual and Allen the Keynotes.

questions.q: The main source of the symptoms recorded in homoeopathic Materia Medica is:
opts: provings of drugs on healthy human beings
questions.why: Materia Medica is built chiefly from provings on healthy people, supplemented by toxicology and clinical observation.

questions.q: Which remedy is described as the chronic of Ignatia?
questions.why: Natrum mur. is the chronic of Ignatia; both cover ailments from grief, with Natrum mur. for the deep, long-standing state.

questions.q: Which remedy is inimical to Phosphorus and should not be given immediately before or after it?
questions.why: Causticum and Phosphorus are inimical. Arsenicum album is complementary to Phosphorus.

questions.q: Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Pulsatilla?
questions.why: Silicea is the chronic of Pulsatilla. The two share a yielding, mild temperament and similar discharges.

questions.q: Aggravation from the slightest motion, with relief from pressure and from lying on the painful side, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Bryonia is worse from any motion and better from pressure. Rhus tox has the opposite modality, better from continued motion.

questions.q: A feeling that the heart will stop beating unless the patient keeps moving is a keynote of:
questions.why: Gelsemium fears the heart will stop unless he moves. Digitalis has the reverse: the heart will stop if he moves.

questions.q: Complaints of sudden, violent onset after exposure to dry, cold wind, with intense fear of death and restlessness, call for:
questions.why: Aconite: sudden onset after dry cold wind, fear of death, anxiety and restlessness. Belladonna is sudden too, but marked by heat, redness and throbbing.

questions.q: Intolerance of milk in infants, with the milk vomited in large curds soon after feeding, indicates:
questions.why: Aethusa's keynote is inability to digest milk, vomited in curds, followed by exhaustion and sleep.

questions.q: After an injury the patient says nothing is the matter with him, the bed feels too hard, and the whole body feels sore and bruised. The remedy is:
questions.why: Arnica: sore, bruised feeling, the bed feels too hard, and the patient insists he is well.

questions.q: In a typhoid state the patient feels his body is scattered about the bed and tries to gather the pieces together. The remedy is:
questions.why: This delusion is the classic keynote of Baptisia, alongside dusky face, offensive discharges and stupor.

questions.q: One cheek red and hot, the other pale and cold; the child is extremely irritable during dentition and wants to be carried. The remedy is:
questions.why: Chamomilla: one cheek red, the other pale, intolerable irritability and pain, quieted only by being carried.

questions.q: Constant nausea that is not relieved by vomiting, with a clean tongue, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Ipecac: persistent nausea, vomiting gives no relief, and the tongue stays clean. Antimonium crudum has a thick white tongue.

questions.q: For punctured wounds where the injured part is cold to the touch yet relieved by cold applications, the indicated remedy is:
questions.why: The remedy is Ledum palustre, which is not among options A to D. Coldness of the part with relief from cold is its keynote.

questions.q: Agonising colic that is relieved by bending double and by hard pressure, often brought on by anger, calls for:
questions.why: Colocynth: colic better bending double and from hard pressure, often after anger. Dioscorea is better from bending backwards.

questions.q: Profuse, painless, gushing diarrhoea that is worse in the early morning suggests:
questions.why: Podophyllum: profuse, painless, gushing, offensive stools, worse early morning. Veratrum album has diarrhoea with collapse and cold sweat.

questions.q: Stiffness and pain that are worse on first motion, better from continued motion and worse in cold, damp weather point to:
questions.why: Rhus tox: the rusty-gate modality, worse on beginning to move, better by continued motion, worse from damp cold.

questions.q: A left-sided neuralgic headache that rises and falls with the sun is characteristic of:
questions.why: Spigelia covers left-sided neuralgia increasing and decreasing with the sun. Sanguinaria has the right-sided version.

questions.q: Ailments from suppressed anger and indignation, along with clean incised wounds, call for:
questions.why: Staphisagria: effects of suppressed anger, humiliation or indignation, and incised wounds, including surgical ones.

questions.q: Burning pains relieved by heat, great anxiety and restlessness, aggravation after midnight, and thirst for small quantities at short intervals indicate:
questions.why: These are the classic generals of Arsenicum album, together with prostration out of proportion to the illness.

questions.q: Desire for cold drinks, which are vomited as soon as they become warm in the stomach, is a keynote of:
questions.why: Phosphorus craves cold drinks and vomits them once they warm in the stomach.

questions.q: Coarse rattling of mucus in the chest with very little expectoration is characteristic of:
questions.why: Antimonium tart.: loud rattling, little expectoration, drowsiness and weakness, especially in children and the old.

questions.q: Anticipatory anxiety with hurriedness, and a craving for sweets which disagree and cause diarrhoea, indicate:
questions.why: Argentum nitricum: hurried, anxious before events, craves sweets, which bring on flatulence and diarrhoea.

questions.q: Extreme chilliness, so that the patient wants the head covered even in summer, with offensive discharges and despair of recovery, calls for:
questions.why: Psorinum is very chilly, wants warm clothing in summer, has filthy-smelling discharges and despairs of recovery. Sulphur is a hot patient.

questions.q: In septic states, a pulse out of proportion to the temperature is the keynote of:
questions.why: Pyrogenium, prepared from decomposed meat, covers septic fevers with a pulse that does not match the temperature.
